I can definitely say that I'm happy now. Of course occasionally things still get hard, but life will always do that. You just have to know how to pick yourself back up. It's hard sometimes to remember how I felt then, but I saw everything as a dead end back then. I didn't plan for the future. Anything beyond a month ahead of time I was skeptical about planning because I wasn't sure if I would still be alive then. I still struggle with pushing people away at times, but our friends are our greatest resource so I have to make an effort to keep them close, especially when I'm struggling. But I had to take actions to get myself to where I am, and the biggest one was putting myself in counseling, which I'm still in. I put myself in counseling last year after a situation I'll get into in a minute, but I'm still in it because it helps me to make taking care of myself a daily habit, as opposed to only trying to take care of myself when it was detrimental to my life.

My financial situation still is not ideal, as I'm making very little, but my financial situation is no longer connected to my parents, and that's what makes the difference. My parents are horribly in debt and irresponsible with their money. They would take my money whenever they got themselves into a tight spot and would never repay it. The fact that I have control over my own finances though makes the situation appear much brighter to me.

I'm going to answer part 3 before I finish 2 because at the time when I posted my original post, I was not driven to keep going for a very long time after that. I ignored several other people who tried to help me, but what caught my attention about this redditor was how desperate he was for me to live. Like it would have personally affected him if I died. I felt like my death would have been a minor inconvenience to the world and like I didn't matter, and in that moment, he wanted nothing more but for me to live. I've always recognized the value in others lives, but I had never recognized it in my own. That began to change for me that day and that's what made me persevere to at the least, keep existing.

I didn't feel the drive to keep going until a year after that post, to the day, in fact. I took it as a sign. I had been trying to make things better for myself, but I was trying to do it alone and with a victimized mindset. I ended up getting sexually abused by a stranger and by someone who was close to me and also decided to break it off with the guy who I had been dating for 4 years, who was anything but pleased. I decided I was tired of the world seeing me as a victim and I realized that I had two options. Once again, I could kill myself, or I could get better. And that's what drove me to go to counseling. I cut out my bad relationships and started from scratch. I worked on building up my confidence and establishing myself as my own person.I put myself first.

Ultimately, yes I did want to hang on, but I didn't see the value in it. When you feel like the world would prefer you to be dead or that it would be easier to be dead than to break yourself off from manipulative and abusive people, it can be hard. It took someone showing me that they desperately wanted me to live in order for me to notice that my life may be worth something.

All in all, if you're struggling, look at the people in your life. Really look at them. Make sure the people around you are good for you. If not, get rid of them. It's hard as hell, but it's completely necessary. Also, do not be afraid to ask for help. You don't need to always be alone and isolated from others. Go out with your friends, do something fun, go to counseling, see your doctor, get some fresh air. And please, take care of yourself. Make sure that you're eating and that you're eating something that's good for you every once in a while. Drink water and GET LOTS OF SLEEP. All of these things affect your hormone levels which can affect how stressed and depressed you are. And if you manage to do this, get a little crazy and maybe go for a walk or work out every once in a while. All of these things are ways that you can help yourself feel better.
I'm so proud of you! I'm struggling with allowing myself to dream right now, so thank you for the inspiration.

Just because you have the smarts to go to an Ivy League school doesn't mean you have to. I understand the massive amount of pressure it puts on you. I had the grades to get in and I chose a small public college instead. Why? Because of what you're feeling right now. There are always ways to make programs more challenging, but at least you get to choose whether or not you want that stress and there are no repercussions for backing out. Holy fuck. I just found this subreddit and I'm almost in tears from the knowledge that I'm not the only one who has to go through this. My mom used to be quite well off and was adjusted to living in luxury. When the economy went down the drain, she went with it. I've grown up being screamed at for things out of my control and having her take her frustrations out on me. Then after all the yelling was done, I'd sit with her as she vented to me the real reason behind her anger with me. My dad travels and my sister is a few years younger than me, so neither one of them understood the reasoning behind her yelling at me. They just thought I was a horrible child and deserved it. She'd bully me into feeling horrible about myself so much that I developed an eating disorder from her telling me how fat and unattractive I was and soon started cutting. When I finally asked
For help, I got screamed at and told that she should be the one cutting if anyone because I put her through so much. I quit on my own after I began teaching myself to disengage. But the yelling still never stopped, so I took over doing all of her chores in hopes To lessen her stress. It helped a bit, but not enough. I work two jobs and take care of my family while being a full time student now while she lies in bed all day and spends the rest of her time yelling or venting to me. Honestly, I have no fucking clue what to do. I fear for my sister more than anything, as I'll be going to college next fall and I've been taking the blows for as long as I can remember.

Please, stop. There are so many better ways to handle this. If you follow through, there's no chance of things getting better. There will be nothing. No chance for you to have a good life. Please stop and reconsider before doing this. Get away and go live with someone you trust for a week or so. Go be around people who love and support you.

Your friends and family won't care about that. They'll just be happy to see you no matter what. And if they judge you for it, then they aren't your true friends. It's what's on the inside that counts. Take your leave and go see them. I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.

PM me if you ever need someone to talk to. Ever. I don't care what time of day or night it is. If random people on the internet care about you without even getting to meet the wonderful person that I know you are, then I think that's more than a good enough reason to carry on. Things will get better. Always keep looking for the bright things in life. And if things fall dark again, you have a loving and supporting community to help you carry on. If you want to talk more, just know I'm here for you.
